subject: Deployment fit and quickstart options for FinLytics

Subject: Deployment fit and quickstart options for FinLytics

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can validate the best deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) for the fraud scoring integration you demoed.

Key notes from our call:
- Primary requirement: sub-100ms median latency for single-score calls at 150 requests/sec sustained; occasional spikes to 800 rps during batch processing windows.
- Data residency: US-only logs; PII payloads must never be stored beyond 30 days.
- Security: customer-managed keys preferred but not blocker for PoC.
- Integration: will call Redwood via a microservice in your VPC; initial traffic will be alpha (sandbox) -> pilot -> prod.

Options we recommend for evaluation:
1) Hosted API (fastest onboarding): sandbox endpoints, token-scoped keys, built-in prefix caching. Good if you want to validate model output quickly; we can meet latency with a proper endpoint mapping and rate slicing for your pattern.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale. Consider if you expect sustained >500 rps and need SLA-backed latency.
3) Private VPC (on-prem/VPC): required if you need full network isolation and KMS/HSM integration for keys. Longer setup but meets strict compliance windows.

Proposed immediate next steps (feel free to edit):
- We’ll provision a sandbox Hosted endpoint and a low-cost dedicated pool estimate; Rishi will provide a quickstart ops checklist (attachments).
- You share a 30-minute preflight (network and auth) — Anita, could you send the internal network contact?
- Internal owners: Marissa will track procurement signals; Rishi will run the perf check during sandbox pilot; I’ll coordinate the timeline and success criteria.

Attachments: FinLytics_quickstart_playbook.pdf (alpha/Pilot steps), network_requirements.xlsx (egress/firewall checklist)

Thanks — I’ll queue a slot for a sandbox in our next provisioning wave.

—

Great questions — answers below, plus concrete handoffs.

1) Hosted API retention and PII: By default Hosted endpoints do not persist customer input in long-term storage. We capture minimal telemetry (token counts, latency histograms) for 30 days; application payloads are not stored unless you opt into logging. For PoC we can enable no-logging mode and mask payloads. If you need customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest, that pushes toward Private VPC but isn’t required for Hosted sandbox.

2) Moving Hosted -> Dedicated mid-pilot: model/version pinning is supported — routing policies allow warm migration with Canary routing. We typically perform a zero-downtime cutover using a traffic-split (5% -> 20% -> 100%) over a 24–48hr window. No forced downtime; you will see transient latency differences during warmup which Rishi will quantify in the perf run.

3) Burst handling and rate-slicing: Hosted enforces per-endpoint rate limits but supports burst windows. For your pattern we recommend:
  - Primary endpoint: steady 150 rps with a 10% headroom SLA
  - Secondary burst endpoint: reserved for batch windows (800 rps) with pre-provisioned burst units for predictable latency
  - Prefix/KV caching for repeat contexts to reduce token counts during spike windows
We’ll propose an endpoint mapping doc and rate-slice values after Rishi captures a short trace sample.

Handoffs & next steps:
- Rishi: I’ve asked you to attach the perf/ops checklist (small runbook) and a short script we’ll run against Hosted sandbox to capture latency distribution.
- Anita: once you share your infra contact we’ll send the network_requirements.xlsx. This includes IP ranges, TLS requirements, and egress rules.
- Marissa: I flagged procurement triggers and the initial pricing estimate for a low-cost dedicated pool (CC: you) so we can fast-track if the pilot requires it.

I attached the quickstart_playbook.pdf and network_requirements.xlsx for your team. Looking at availability — we can provision sandbox endpoints Wed (Jul 9) or Fri (Jul 11). Which works for you?
